Field / question: What are you trying to make the system do?
Why it matters: Defines the intended operation and prevents answers to a different problem.
Common missing-information failure: Threads start with a product name or error but omit the desired physical or scientific outcome.
Suggested response format: One or two sentences with the intended end state.
Example: Move ten plates from the hotel to the reader, read each once, then return them to storage.

Field / question: Instrument manufacturer, model, serial family, and relevant modules
Why it matters: Interface, geometry, firmware, and recovery behavior differ across models and modules.
Common missing-information failure: Advice assumes the wrong device generation or accessory.
Suggested response format: Manufacturer + exact model + installed modules.
Example: Tecan Fluent 1080 with FCA and LPT220 integration.

Field / question: Control software, version, edition, operating system, and licence features
Why it matters: Major versions can replace APIs, file semantics, and licensed capabilities.
Common missing-information failure: A legacy COM answer is applied to a REST-era system, or a driver is present but not licensed.
Suggested response format: Exact version strings and enabled options.
Example: VENUS 6.2; REST API enabled; Windows 11.

Field / question: Firmware versions for instrument and connected devices
Why it matters: Registers, commands, sensor behavior, and driver compatibility can be firmware-specific.
Common missing-information failure: Model-specific register maps or obsolete firmware tools are conflated.
Suggested response format: Version or diagnostic-screen output.
Example: STR240 V2.13; PLC firmware 1.08.

Field / question: How is the device being controlled?
Why it matters: A device can expose vendor APIs, serial protocols, REST, COM, file exchange, or GUI automation with different guarantees.
Common missing-information failure: A user says 'driver' without identifying the actual interface layer.
Suggested response format: API/SDK/protocol/driver name and connection medium.
Example: REST over localhost; RS-232 through USB adapter.

Field / question: What licences, SDKs, manuals, or credentials are available?
Why it matters: Nominally available drivers or APIs may be unusable without feature licences or restricted documentation.
Common missing-information failure: Advice assumes access to a commercial development kit or manual.
Suggested response format: Available / unavailable / uncertain for each item.
Example: Driver Framework installed; licence unavailable; service manual unavailable.

Field / question: Method, script, worklist, or project version
Why it matters: Without immutable method identity, two runs or machines cannot be compared.
Common missing-information failure: Discussion cites a filename with no commit, version, checksum, or export date.
Suggested response format: Commit/tag/version plus checksum when possible.
Example: Method v1.7.2, Git commit 1a2b3c4.

Field / question: Libraries, submethods, liquid classes, labware files, drivers
Why it matters: External dependencies can change behavior without changing the main method file.
Common missing-information failure: Only the top-level method is shared.
Suggested response format: Versioned list or deployment manifest.
Example: HSL library 4.1; liquid class LC-Serum-2026-02; plate definition rev 3.

Field / question: Deck layout, carrier/site assignment, positions, lids, seals, nesting
Why it matters: Geometry and physical state determine collision, reachability, and transfer validity.
Common missing-information failure: A destination lid, wrong site, or missing nesting offset appears only during execution.
Suggested response format: Annotated layout or exported configuration; redact sensitive sample names.
Example: Plate A on carrier 3/site 2 with lid assigned; tip rack at site 5.

Field / question: Manufacturer, catalogue number, lot, definition source, and local modifications
Why it matters: Nominally similar labware can differ in dimensions, materials, tolerances, or imported semantics.
Common missing-information failure: A generic name such as '96-well plate' hides the actual resource.
Suggested response format: Part number + lot + source of software definition.
Example: Corning 3603, lot X; PLR definition commit abc123.

Field / question: Which dimensions or coordinate semantics are measured, declared, or inferred?
Why it matters: Physical models can contain wrong z origins, skirt assumptions, or imported offsets.
Common missing-information failure: A value is treated as authoritative without provenance.
Suggested response format: Field + value + unit + provenance + measurement procedure.
Example: Plate height 14.35 mm, measured with calipers, n=3.

Field / question: Liquid identity, viscosity/conductivity, volume range, temperature, surface behavior
Why it matters: Transfer performance depends on material properties beyond command syntax.
Common missing-information failure: Advice proposes flow rates without identifying the liquid regime.
Suggested response format: Liquid class, composition, temperature, source/destination volumes.
Example: 50% glycerol, 20 °C, 8 µL aspiration from 40 µL start volume.

Field / question: Timing windows, sample stability, contamination limits, cell-layer or assay constraints
Why it matters: A technically executable schedule or transfer can still be scientifically invalid.
Common missing-information failure: The scheduler optimizes waiting time without sample-expiry or assay constraints.
Suggested response format: Explicit bounds and acceptance rules.
Example: Read within 15 minutes of incubation; no more than 1% carryover.

Field / question: What exactly should happen?
Why it matters: A precise expected state is necessary to distinguish error, unsupported behavior, and user expectation.
Common missing-information failure: The thread reports 'does not work' without an expected command, state, or measurement.
Suggested response format: Ordered expected events and final disposition.
Example: Aspirate 100 µL, dispense to plate B, update both volume states, then eject tips.

Field / question: What happened instead?
Why it matters: Separates direct observation from diagnosis or speculation.
Common missing-information failure: The post contains only the presumed root cause.
Suggested response format: Chronological observed events; label interpretations separately.
Example: Pickup and aspiration completed; dispense raised LidPresentError.

Field / question: Full error text, timestamp, log excerpt, trace, screenshot, or sensor curve
Why it matters: Exact evidence enables first-divergence localization and version-specific diagnosis.
Common missing-information failure: Paraphrased error messages remove decisive identifiers.
Suggested response format: Paste text where possible; include timestamp and run ID.
Example: 2026-07-28 14:02:11, LidPresentError, step 37.

Field / question: Run ID, configuration identity, resource identity, and relevant timestamps
Why it matters: Evidence must be connected to the same run and deployment.
Common missing-information failure: Logs, screenshots, and methods come from different attempts.
Suggested response format: Single run bundle or explicit mapping.
Example: Run R-00412 used manifest M-1.7.2 and plate lot X.

Field / question: What actions completed and where is every material/resource now?
Why it matters: Software rollback cannot reverse aspiration, dispensing, motion, or heating.
Common missing-information failure: The thread says the run failed without recording material in tips or plate positions.
Suggested response format: Last confirmed action + uncertain fields + material disposition.
Example: Tips contain approximately 100 µL; source volume reduced; destination unchanged.

Field / question: What did the operator or system do next?
Why it matters: Manual actions can alter state, contamination history, and scientific validity.
Common missing-information failure: A successful continuation is reported without the recovery sequence.
Suggested response format: Chronological actions with actor and timestamps.
Example: Operator returned tips to source using custom abort handler, then discarded tips.

Field / question: What checks, simulations, measurements, or reproductions were run?
Why it matters: Prevents repeated suggestions and reveals the deepest validation stage reached.
Common missing-information failure: A simulation pass is presented without stating that no wet test occurred.
Suggested response format: Test object, environment, acceptance rule, result.
Example: Simulation trace matched; dry motion not run; wet test not run.

Field / question: What would count as resolved or valid?
Why it matters: A test result is uninterpretable without a threshold or expected invariant.
Common missing-information failure: A curve 'looks better' but no acceptable transfer error is defined.
Suggested response format: Numerical threshold or explicit invariant.
Example: Transferred volume within ±5%; no unexpected liquid-history conflict.

Field / question: What changed in software, firmware, hardware, method, labware, liquid, or environment?
Why it matters: Recent changes are high-value causal candidates.
Common missing-information failure: The user omits a version upgrade, new lot, or re-teaching.
Suggested response format: Dated change list.
Example: Upgraded VENUS 4 to 6; changed tip lot; re-taught carrier 2.

Field / question: Does the issue reproduce on another machine, user, method, lot, or configuration?
Why it matters: Independent reproduction raises evidence grade and distinguishes local calibration from portable defects.
Common missing-information failure: A single-machine success is treated as a universal definition.
Suggested response format: Matrix of tested configurations and outcomes.
Example: Fails on machine B; works on A; same software and tip lot.

Field / question: What cannot be shared, and are there safety or sample-value constraints?
Why it matters: Redaction and recovery decisions depend on confidentiality, hazards, and sample consequence.
Common missing-information failure: Users omit key context because they do not know how to share it safely.
Suggested response format: State constraints without revealing sensitive assay details.
Example: Sample is irreplaceable; composition confidential; safe to share viscosity range.

Field / question: What response would be most useful?
Why it matters: Distinguishes diagnosis, comparison, code review, design feedback, or a recovery procedure.
Common missing-information failure: Replies solve a different problem than the user intended.
Suggested response format: Choose one primary request and optional secondary request.
Example: Primary: diagnose root cause. Secondary: propose a reproducible test.
